text:
The training–inference mismatch is established, but terminal masking is already part of original BERT4Rec: its paper explicitly adds training samples with only the last item masked, alongside random Cloze masking, and appends a mask for inference. Thus, joint interior/terminal training is a grounded refinement rather than a new objective. [BERT4Rec, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690v2). Recency Sampling (2022) argues that random item masking is weakly aligned with sequential recommendation and can require longer training; its experiments do not establish that a particular mixed objective improves this BERT4Rec benchmark. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643).

Recent related work supports exploring complementary objectives: Masked History Learning (2025; revised 2026) combines historical reconstruction with future prediction in generative recommenders, while Q-BERT4Rec (2025; revised 2026) proposes span, tail and multi-region masking within a substantially different multimodal framework. Neither directly validates random-prefix terminal masking for the supplied ID-based BERT4Rec. [MHL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23649), [Q-BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02474).

Actionable hypothesis: within one shared BERT4Rec per category, mix interior-mask reconstruction with random-prefix examples ending in a reserved mask; the terminal target and all later interactions must be absent from that example’s input. Compare interior-only, terminal-only and mixed training under matched compute, fixed seeds and unchanged appended-mask inference. For left padding, read the final nonpadding mask position. Select by the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; lower training loss or larger margins alone cannot establish improved generalization.
